# Ascendancies

_Generated from PoB tree data `3.29`. Regenerate after any data update - this script
rebuilds `ascendancies.db` too._

Every class, ascendancy, Bloodline and node lives in `data/ascendancies.db`; this file
holds the rules. A node name from memory is a hypothesis - query it; zero rows means
it does not exist.

## Points

Primary and secondary ascendancies share **one pool of 8 points**. A point spent on
a Bloodline is a point not spent on the class, which is why both are in one dataset.

`CountAllocNodes` (`PassiveSpec.lua:822`) returns `used, ascUsed, secondaryAscUsed`.
`ascUsed` counts **every** node with an `ascendancyName`, Bloodline nodes included;
`secondaryAscUsed` re-counts the Bloodline subset. `Build.lua:908` warns when
`ascUsed > 8`, and separately when `secondaryAscUsed > 8`, so the total binds.
Trust the warning and check `ascUsed` on every build.

Nodes with `free=1` are `isMultipleChoiceOption`, which `CountAllocNodes` skips -
they are a choice attached to another node rather than a purchase.

## Selection

Primary: `build.spec:SelectClass(class_id)` then `build.spec:SelectAscendClass(asc_id)`.
Secondary: `build.spec:SelectSecondaryAscendClass(asc_id)` with a `kind='bloodline'`
`asc_id` - the call does no class check, so any class may take any Bloodline.

Attribute affinity is the class's own starting attributes - a property of the class,
not of the ascendancy. Bloodlines have no affinity; their start node sits in a
detached group of its own.

## Querying ascendancies.db

Run `sqlite3` with paths from the repo root (from `src/`, prefix `../`).

- `classes(id, name, base_str, base_dex, base_int, affinity)` - `id` is the
  `SelectClass` argument.
- `ascendancies(id, name, kind, class_id, asc_id, tree_key)` - kind `class|bloodline`;
  `asc_id` is the `SelectAscendClass` / `SelectSecondaryAscendClass` argument
  (per-class for kind=class, global for bloodlines); `class_id` NULL for bloodlines;
  `tree_key` is the `ascendancyName` raw tree nodes carry.
- `nodes(id, ascendancy_id, name, free)` - `id` is the tree node id; `free=1` = no
  point cost (see Points).
- `node_stats(node_id, ord, line, template)` - a node's stat lines in order;
  `template` has every number as `#` - LIKE-match on it, not on `line`.
- `meta(key, value)` - `tree_version`, `generated_at`.

Canonical queries:

```sh
DB=.claude/skills/cook/data/ascendancies.db
# classes with their ascendancies and selection ids
sqlite3 $DB "SELECT c.name, c.id, a.asc_id, a.name FROM ascendancies a
  JOIN classes c ON c.id=a.class_id ORDER BY c.id, a.asc_id;"
# every node of one ascendancy, stats inline
sqlite3 $DB "SELECT n.name, n.free, s.line FROM nodes n
  JOIN ascendancies a ON a.id=n.ascendancy_id
  LEFT JOIN node_stats s ON s.node_id=n.id
  WHERE a.name='Slayer' ORDER BY n.name, s.ord;"
# who grants a mechanic - search templates across all ascendancies
sqlite3 $DB "SELECT a.name, n.name, s.line FROM node_stats s
  JOIN nodes n ON n.id=s.node_id JOIN ascendancies a ON a.id=n.ascendancy_id
  WHERE s.template LIKE '%Culling Strike%';"
```
